newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan sugar refinery appoints new head.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan sugar refinery appoints new head.

text.p: Morocco's main sugar refinery Cosumar, a subsidiary of ONA conglomerate appointed Lekbir Belaidi as new managing director, ONA group said on Wednesday.
Belaidi replaced Noureddine Benmakhlouf, the group said.
Casablanca-based Cosumar sugar complex posted a net profit of 223.6 million dirhams ($23.6 million), up 43.6 percent from 155.7 million dirhams in 1995, the added.
ONA, Morocco's largest private conglomerate, announced on Tuesday the launch of a new refinery aimed at increasing capacity and improving the quality of its products.
"The new refinery, which will provide the domestic market with a better sugar products, is expected to be operational in June 1997," the group chairman Fouad Filali said.
The new plant which was built in the same area where Cosumar is located already underwent its first technical tests, a Moroccan trader said.
No figures for the new refinery capacity were immediately available.
Cosumar refines an average 2,000 tonnes of raw sugar per day. It imported more than 500,000 tonnes of raw sugar in 1996 or nearly 50 percent of the country's consumption.
"There was a relative stagnation of Cosumar activity which led to a slight rise of its consolidated turnover by 0.8 percent to 3.14 billion dirhams in 1996," Filali told reporters.
ONA group consolidated turnover dropped 2.5 percent to 18.11 billion dirhams in 1996 "translating the priority given by the group to the profitability issue," Filali added.
